metric: Incremental models that do equal their full refresh under a stated contract (watermark append and merge, key de-duplication, day watermarks, group re-aggregation, joins to unchanged tables); a case no rule covers is left unknown, never called safe or different.
caveats: Rules R3-R6 (de-duplication, day watermark, re-aggregation, unchanged joined tables) were written for the 4 dev unknowns they now prove, so the dev number is optimistic; held-out cases were not used. One dev case (pre-operation reload window) was relabelled from safe to diverges: two new rows more than 2 hours apart in one run lose the earlier one, which insert_new allows. R2 used to prove a filtered merge under updates, which diverges; no case in the corpus hit it. Proofs assume the COALESCE default precedes every event time, the declared source key is unique and non-NULL, and a re-aggregated group column is never NULL. Baseline before generalising the rules: 2/13 safe cases proven on the first 37 cases.
correctness: 0 false proofs: no proven case diverges in the simulator, the scripted workloads or a 25-sequence search (tests/test_incremental.py)
held_out: 3/3 proven, 0 wrong (3 safe among the 12 blind cases)
